value: the development of physical relaxation techniques in Britain from the interwar period to the founding of Relaxation for Living in 1972
how physical relaxation became a teachable therapeutic skill and the frameworks that let a relaxation charity form in 1970s Britain
an account of how relaxation practitioners created and answered demand for individualistic health-management strategies

quote: This article explores the origins and development of “physical relaxation” techniques and ideologies, starting in the interwar period, and the development of practical, therapeutic, social and cultural frameworks necessary for such an organization to come into being in 1970s Britain.

This analysis highlights the role that relaxation practitioners played in both creating and responding to demand for individualistic health-management strategies, many of which have shaped contemporary health and wellbeing agendas.

Implicit and recurrent in this history of relaxation therapy is the concept of “balance”. Key therapeutic goals of relaxation have been to balance overactive minds and bodies
Until the 1960s, “hypertension” had been a disputed medical category, and the term was not used exclusively to relate to blood pressure.

It was deemed especially relevant to men’s health through the construction of hypertension as a key “risk factor”, the framing of middle-aged working men comprising the most “at risk” population, and the developing discourse of “stress”.

Belief that the strain of modern living took its toll on physical and mental health was not particular to the middle decades of the twentieth century, but the growing discourse of “stress” allowed for a rapid proliferation of this idea and the development of associated therapeutic interventions, such as relaxation.
